A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FastVAR work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends after the references; v3 includes supplementary Sections A–H. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FastVAR generation-quality, latency, memory and pruning-ablation results in Section 4, Tables 1–5 and associated figures.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and additionally reports ImageNet evaluations, preference scores, module profiling, cache-step ablations and extreme-pruning experiments.

M1.justification: The pivotal-token selection, cached-token restoration, cache source and progressive pruning procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing operations; applying FastVAR to ImageNet does not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds 256×256 class-conditional generation on ImageNet, extending beyond v1's text-conditioned GenEval/MJHQ30K evaluations and zero-shot larger-resolution generation. This introduces a distinct conditioning task and image population.

E2.justification: Table A.1 adds comparisons with VAR at depths 24 and 30 and CoDe at N=8 and N=9. CoDe was discussed but not quantitatively compared in v1. The main comparison methods remain unchanged; Infinite and Infinity denote the same backbone.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include the ImageNet model configurations and IS/precision/recall metrics, HPSv2.1 and ImageReward scoring, 75% pruning for module profiling, and controlled cache-step and extreme-pruning tests. These substantially extend the evaluation protocol; the existing Section 4.1 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained pruning-ratio and scale-sensitivity analyses, v3 adds a cache-source sweep in Table A.4, a HART extreme-pruning test in Table A.3, and attention/FFN speedups and PTS/CTR overhead profiling in Figure A.1. These directly examine previously undocumented design choices, failure conditions and computational costs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added tables continue single-value reporting.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results. Newly reported results include ImageNet FastVAR(d=24) at 1.1 seconds and FID 2.64, HART FastVAR HPSv2.1 of 27.85 versus ToMe's 27.04, and FID 48.54 for HART's extreme-pruning configuration. Cache-sweep results, module timings and additional generated examples further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical formulation remain unchanged. The supplement adds empirical analyses and implementation pseudocode, without substantive new definitions, assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free cached token pruning, compatibility with FlashAttention, the reported 2.7× speedup with negligible quality loss, and zero-shot higher-resolution generation.

C2.justification: Building on v1's early-scale sensitivity and backbone-dependence caveats, Appendices A and D–F expand explanations of low-resolution limitations and cache proximity. They also hypothesize that model size explains extreme-pruning tolerance and discuss adaptive or layer-wise pruning as future work.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 supplies previously absent PyTorch-like pseudocode for pooling, scoring, token selection, interpolation and restoration. The existing hardware disclosure, default pruning schedules, VAE timing exclusion and code-access link are unchanged. Detailed sampling protocols for the additional benchmarks remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including IntLoRA, Follow Your Pose, Follow-your-emoji, test-time compute scaling, HPSv2 and ImageReward. These provide limited additional context; the central positioning relative to diffusion acceleration, token merging and CoDe remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section organization remain essentially unchanged. Edits include correcting Infinite to Infinity in much of the paper and adding corresponding-author/project-lead notes. Supplementary Sections A–H extend the exposition without extensively rewriting the existing text.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with Tables A.1–A.4, a module-timing chart, an algorithm display, intermediate-generation strips, paired output galleries and larger-resolution examples in Figures A.1–A.7. The main figures and tables retain their organization, with limited label changes.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark evaluations and cache/extreme-pruning ablations better support applicability and failure boundaries, while the pseudocode supplies documentation referenced but absent in v1. The benefit is limited by sparse new evaluation details and reporting errors: Appendix B calls 0.59+0.24 ms 0.63 ms, and Appendix D claims superiority on every metric despite Table A.4's two-object scores. The additional evidence nevertheless provides a modest net improvement in empirical completeness and practical guidance.
